notes.title: PATCH 0.4.0
notes.notes:
Yes, it took a little longer than expected, but it's finally here. LAST MINI BOSS COMPLETED. With this major stage completed, I can now focus on the final stretch of the game, which involves alternative game modes, a mission system for the main story, and a final final boss, among others. The "Informal Roadmap" that I mentioned in the last post will be explained in a simple and direct way: goals.

Now that I've managed to finish the last mini boss of the initial gameplay loop, I can calmly focus on the next stages, which will probably take longer to complete, namely:

MAIN STORY

It will be based on a mission system. It will be used exclusively to conclude the game's narrative. The player will have fixed objectives that they will have to complete during their game in order to unlock the main story route. The game's Final Boss will be completed together with the release of the story mode missions. Once the player finishes this part, there will be additional content in the location used to complete these missions.

OPTIMIZATION

I am aware of performance issues that we have encountered in the current state of the game, and so I intend to do a general review of the code for the entire combat part to identify the cause and make the game as optimized as possible. Better optimization means that a wider audience can enjoy the game, including players on portable devices such as the Steam Deck. As it stands at the moment, it runs with extremely fluctuating performance, hence my emphasis on this optimization part.

NEW GAME MODES

- New game modes. Considered so far, in addition to the current one of going to wave 100:

- Infinite Mode;
- Hardcore Mode;
- Darkness Mode;

The new game modes will be added as additional after the completion of other game priorities.

I won't give dates so as not to commit to deadlines I can't meet, but my goal is to at least have the main story completed by the end of December. I might finish it sooner, or I might finish it later. But I'll do my best to meet my estimate.

notes.title: UPDATE - 0.3.0
notes.notes:
"Wait, shouldn't this be version 0.2.4?" Yes and no. (more yes than no). I'll explain everything at the end of this post if you're interested. But first...

I worked like crazy to bring this new addition to the game as quickly as possible and with as few issues as possible...


NEW BOSS

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44843544/807a1c7f911da54443d63b184665d9ebfa51bdfa.png


Don't expect too much complexity in its mechanics, but I guarantee it will be more engaging than the only mini-boss that has been available until now. With a bigger variety, my intention of making the gameplay more random is coming to life. Instead of always facing the same boss, you might encounter a different one. That sense of not having control over certain aspects of the game is what fascinates me the most in this genre, and executing it in a fun way is my biggest goal. From concept to execution, the mechanics of this boss took me about 2 weeks, requiring more time for full implementation.

The next planned content will be: Hardcore Difficulty (if you thought it was hard already, get ready) and a new mini-boss. I’m not sure about the order of implementation, but this will definitely be my next focus. 

Now for the explanation:

Since this is my first project, I don’t have much experience or knowledge about how to properly catalog the game's versions, so I opted for a simpler format to understand. Smaller updates will increase the version by 0.0.1, while significant changes will jump by 0.1.0 (hence the leap to 0.3.0). Since this is a “new” version, I decided to register it as 0.3.0 instead of 0.2.4, as I believe the changes warrant a version jump.

All past and future updates serve both for me (as the developer) and for players or future players, allowing them to follow the game's development progress in detail if they're interested. Honestly, it helps me a lot to stay focused. My plan is to bump the version by 0.1.0 whenever something significant is added, such as additional content or a new game mode. The goal is to follow this pattern until I reach the long-awaited version 1.0.0 (the official release), where I’ll have successfully completed the game and made it as polished as possible.

Note: I’ll be taking a week off after these intense weeks to return at full strength, but any urgent bug or glitch fixes will still be implemented if needed.

notes.notes:
A bit delayed, but what matters is the delivery. I present to you version 0.2.0, which includes changes or additions to mechanics and information that have been missing since the game's launch. Below is everything that was added or fixed in this version. I RECOMMEND taking a quick look at the things that interest you, as not everything is fully explained or intuitive in the game yet. Consider this update as part 1 (functionality), with part 2 (revision) coming in the next update with the necessary improvements.

ACCESSORY EFFECTS

You have no idea how much I wanted to implement this. A unique effect has been created for each accessory, each with its own characteristic to allow combinations with all the cats and staves. I won’t reveal the effects here, as I want you to discover them on your own. If you already have accessories in your save, I recommend checking the game manual in the lobby for their updated descriptions, which now include their effects at the end.

This isn’t described anywhere yet, but some accessories have their effects increased when upgraded. To avoid frustration for those with this functionality, I’ll list the ones that have this: Chief's Hat, Cap, Beret, Top Hat, Clawdalf's Hat. In upcoming updates, I’ll add the effect description and its respective current and next upgrade values in the upgrade area.

SHOP WITH MORE INFORMATION

I noticed a lot of feedback about the high prices of items and took that into consideration with this idea. To make your hard-earned money more valuable, I added a description below the cats’ names so you can get an idea of each cat’s unique ability, even if you haven’t purchased them. Some descriptions might be a bit vague, but at least you’ll have a better understanding of what you’re buying, avoiding potential disappointment from blind purchases. I only added this to the cats because the menu layout wouldn’t allow for more changes without a complete shop menu overhaul.

REROLL SYSTEM

Last but not least, REROLL. You can now use Golden tokens dropped during the match to reroll those sad rolls with things you don’t want or need... for a price, of course. As a base, the cost will be 1 Golden token for rerolls and 2 Golden tokens to increase the rarity of all cards. Note that the cost increases gradually with each use and resets to the base values at the start of the next wave. A certain accessory can help out in this area, enhancing this newly implemented mechanic.
